title: Water for the Last Balcony
original_pitch: A hillside block receives one trickle of water. Each household can keep it or tilt a tile toward the next balcony down. The camera follows the stream all afternoon. On the last balcony a child fills a birdbath, and the bird flies back uphill.
selection_justification: A downhill ribbon connects miniature architecture into a collective action, ending with the bird carrying the movement uphill.
adaptation: Three households open their gates in sequence to pass a trickle through terracotta channels. Water reaches the dry birdbath on the lowest balcony. A bird drinks, then flies back uphill past the opened gates.
story_beats: 4–9 s: three gates pass water downhill
9–11 s: lowest birdbath fills and bird drinks
11–14 s: bird returns uphill above the roofs
music_prompt: Fourteen second instrumental Mediterranean miniature. Nylon guitar harmonics, warm hand percussion, flute and chamber strings. A sparse trickle grows into an interconnected dancing phrase, a gentle pause for a bird at ten seconds, ascending airy final phrase. No voices.
sfx_prompt: A small stream trickles through terracotta channels, three light clay tile taps, water filling a shallow stone birdbath, then one clear small bird chirp and soft wingbeats. No music or speech.
